name: Apple Calendar
description: Apple Calendar is Apple's calendar application and iCloud-backed scheduling service for calendars, events, invitations, attendees, recurrence, availability, alerts, and shared calendars.
agentUseSummary: Apple Calendar cannot yet be connected through Relay. Apple documents native EventKit access with per-device user permission and separately supports account authorization or an app-specific password for compatible third-party iCloud Calendar clients, but it publishes no Relay-ready server API, Calendar OAuth scope, enrollment path, or frozen CalDAV lifecycle contract; the product must choose and validate an authority architecture first.

blocked.label: Connect Apple Calendar
blocked.description: Connect remains unavailable until Relay selects and accepts a supported native or delegated server authority model.

blocked.label: Collect Apple credentials
blocked.description: Apple Account passwords, app-specific passwords, verification codes, cookies, session tokens, and private framework material are never collected.

blocked.label: Read calendars and events
blocked.description: Calendars, events, attendees, invitations, recurrence, availability, locations, notes, URLs, and alarms remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Change calendars or use raw interfaces
blocked.description: Creating, updating, deleting, responding to, or inviting through events, private CalDAV discovery, scraping, device automation, arbitrary endpoints, and raw responses are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Apple Calendar action is enabled before a supported authority architecture and representative acceptance.

runtimeSupport.description: No Apple Calendar wrapper is mounted before the local-versus-server authority architecture is frozen.
No Apple Calendar wrapper is mounted before the local-versus-server authority architecture is frozen.

providerSetup.blocker: Apple's documented native EventKit path runs inside an Apple-platform app and requires explicit per-device calendar permission and sandbox entitlements. Apple's current support guidance also allows compatible third-party apps to authorize iCloud Calendar access with an Apple Account, or fall back to a broad app-specific password, but public developer documentation does not identify Calendar scopes, REST or CalDAV endpoints, client registration, token lifecycle, quotas, or server-to-server semantics for that supported-app flow.
providerSetup.nextAction: The product and security owners should select either a Mac-local EventKit connector with an explicit runtime boundary or a provider-approved server authorization contract. The exclusive acceptance task must then obtain Apple entitlement or enrollment evidence, run consent on a representative account, verify exact calendar-only authority, revocation, schemas, recurrence, invitations, quotas, offline behavior, and disconnect denial, and return the frozen contract before implementation.

evidence.supports: Apple documents native EventKit calendar access and requires applications to request the specific user authorization level they need, with calendar usage descriptions in the app bundle.
Apple states sandboxed macOS apps need the personal-information calendars entitlement to access Calendar data, establishing a local app permission model rather than a Railway server API.

Apple states compatible third-party apps can request Apple Account authorization for iCloud Calendar and users can revoke access through Account Data Sharing, but does not publish a Calendar developer scope or endpoint contract on that page.

Apple documents app-specific passwords as a fallback for apps accessing iCloud Mail, Calendar, and Contacts, requires two-factor authentication, permits up to 25 credentials, and supports individual or global revocation; the credential is not calendar-scoped.
